points.title: 童年与少年时期
points.description: 维克多·雨果于1802年2月26日出生于法国贝桑松，是约瑟夫·雨果和索菲·特雷布谢的第三个儿子。他的父亲是共和党军官，母亲是天主教保皇党人。父母政治立场的对立影响了雨果早期的世界观。1808年，雨果随母亲移居巴黎，开始接受教育。1811年，他跟随父亲前往西班牙，在那里度过了童年时光，这段经历丰富了他的文化视野。1817年，15岁的雨果在法国诗歌竞赛中获得荣誉，展现出非凡的文学天赋。
points.descriptionEn: Victor Hugo was born on February 26, 1802, in Besançon, France, as the third son of Joseph Hugo and Sophie Trébuchet. His father was a Republican officer while his mother was a Catholic Royalist, opposing political views that influenced Hugo's early worldview. In 1808, Hugo moved to Paris with his mother to begin his education. In 1811, he accompanied his father to Spain, where he spent his childhood, an experience that enriched his cultural perspective. By 1817, at just 15 years old, Hugo received honors in a French poetry competition, demonstrating his extraordinary literary talent.

points.title: 浪漫主义崛起
points.description: 1822年，雨果出版第一本诗集《颂歌与杂诗》，获得国王路易十八的年金资助。1827年，他发表戏剧《克伦威尔》，并在序言中提出了浪漫主义文学理论，挑战古典主义传统。1830年，戏剧《欧那尼》上演引发激烈争论，标志着浪漫主义在法国的胜利。1831年，他创作了不朽名著《巴黎圣母院》，这部小说展现了哥特建筑的壮美和社会不公。1833年，他与女演员朱丽叶·德鲁埃开始了一段长达50年的恋情。这一时期，雨果积极参与政治活动，支持自由主义和共和主义思想，成为法国文学界的重要人物。
points.descriptionEn: In 1822, Hugo published his first collection of poems 'Odes and Miscellaneous Poems,' receiving a royal pension from King Louis XVIII. In 1827, he wrote the play 'Cromwell' with a preface that laid out the principles of Romanticist literature, challenging classical traditions. The 1830 premiere of his play 'Hernani' sparked fierce controversy, marking the triumph of Romanticism in France. In 1831, he created his masterpiece 'The Hunchback of Notre-Dame,' showcasing the beauty of Gothic architecture and social injustice. In 1833, he began a 50-year relationship with actress Juliette Drouet. During this period, Hugo actively participated in politics, supporting liberal and republican ideas, becoming a major figure in French literature.

points.title: 政治活动与家庭悲剧
points.description: 1843年，雨果的挚友兼女婿雅克·杜邦在船上溺水身亡，同时他的女儿莱奥波蒂娜与丈夫也遭遇不幸，这些悲剧深深打击了雨果。1845年，他被任命为法兰西学院院士，成为法国文学界的最高荣誉。1848年，他积极参与二月革命，支持第二共和国的建立。1849年，他当选为制宪会议成员，反对死刑，倡导普选权。1850年，他发表《小拿破仑》一书，批判路易·拿破仑的独裁倾向。这一时期，雨果的文学创作有所减少，但政治立场更加鲜明，为后来的流亡生活埋下伏笔。
points.descriptionEn: In 1843, Hugo's close friend and son-in-law Jacques Dupont drowned in a boating accident, while his daughter Léopoldine and her husband also perished, tragedies that deeply affected Hugo. In 1845, he was appointed to the Académie Française, the highest honor in French literature. In 1848, he actively participated in the February Revolution supporting the establishment of the Second Republic. In 1849, he was elected to the Constituent Assembly, opposing the death penalty and advocating for universal suffrage. In 1850, he published 'Napoléon le Petit,' criticizing Louis Napoleon's autocratic tendencies. During this period, Hugo's literary output decreased, but his political stance became more pronounced, setting the stage for his later exile.

points.title: 流亡岁月
points.description: 1851年12月，路易·拿破仑发动政变，成为拿破仑三世，雨果因强烈反对而被迫流亡。他先前往布鲁塞尔，后定居于海峡群岛的泽西岛和根西岛，在那里度过了近20年的流亡生活。流亡期间，雨果创作了大量重要作品，包括《悲惨世界》(1862)、《海上劳工》(1866)和《笑面人》(1869)等。这些作品表达了他对不公正社会的批判和对人类苦难的同情。1862年，《悲惨世界》的出版确立了雨果作为世界级文学大师的地位。尽管远离祖国，雨果仍积极参与政治活动，发表文章谴责拿破仑三世的统治，成为法国反对派的精神领袖。
points.descriptionEn: In December 1851, Louis Napoleon staged a coup d'état, becoming Napoleon III, and Hugo was forced into exile due to his strong opposition. He first went to Brussels, then settled in the Channel Islands of Jersey and Guernsey, where he spent nearly 20 years in exile. During this period, Hugo created numerous major works including 'Les Misérables' (1862), 'Toilers of the Sea' (1866), and 'The Man Who Laughs' (1869). These works expressed his critique of unjust society and sympathy for human suffering. The publication of 'Les Misérables' in 1862 established Hugo as a world literary master. Despite being far from his homeland, Hugo remained politically active, publishing articles condemning Napoleon III's rule and becoming the spiritual leader of the French opposition.

points.title: 回归与晚年
points.description: 1870年，普法战争爆发后，拿破仑三世倒台，雨果得以返回巴黎。他支持巴黎公社，但对公社的暴力行为持保留态度。1872年，他发表《我控诉》，谴责那些曾迫害他的人。1876年，他被选为参议员，继续为民主、自由和正义发声。1883年，他的长期伴侣朱丽叶·德鲁埃去世，这对雨果是沉重打击。1885年5月22日，维克多·雨果在巴黎逝世，享年83岁。法国为他举行了国葬，超过两百万人参加了他的葬礼游行，他的遗体被安葬于先贤祠，成为少数获此殊荣的作家之一。雨果的晚年作品包括《九十三》(1874)等，继续探讨历史、政治和道德问题。
points.descriptionEn: In 1870, with the outbreak of the Franco-Prussian War and the fall of Napoleon III, Hugo returned to Paris. He supported the Paris Commune but maintained reservations about its violent actions. In 1872, he published 'I Accuse,' condemning those who had persecuted him. In 1876, he was elected to the Senate, continuing to advocate for democracy, freedom, and justice. In 1883, his long-time partner Juliette Droue died, a heavy blow to Hugo. On May 22, 1885, Victor Hugo died in Paris at the age of 83. France held a state funeral for him, with over two million people attending his funeral procession. His body was interred in the Panthéon, making him one of the few writers to receive such honor. Hugo's later works included 'Ninety-Three' (1874), continuing to explore historical, political, and moral issues.

points.title: 文学巅峰
points.description: 1845年是雨果文学创作的重要里程碑。他被路易-菲利普国王授予法兰西学院院士称号，这是法国文学界的最高荣誉。同年，他开始创作《悲惨世界》的早期版本，这部作品后来成为他最著名的代表作之一。在这一时期，雨果的文学风格已经完全成熟，他的作品融合了浪漫主义的激情与对社会现实的深刻洞察。他的诗歌、戏剧和小说都展现出惊人的创造力和人文关怀，使他成为法国乃至世界文学史上最重要的作家之一。这一时期的创作奠定了雨果作为浪漫主义文学领袖的地位，也为他后来的政治活动和流亡生活提供了精神支持。
points.descriptionEn: 1845 marked a significant milestone in Hugo's literary career. He was elected to the Académie Française, the highest honor in French literature, by King Louis-Philippe. The same year, he began working on the early version of what would become his most famous work, 'Les Misérables'. During this period, Hugo's literary style had fully matured, with his works blending Romantic passion with profound insight into social reality. His poetry, drama, and novels demonstrated remarkable creativity and human concern, establishing him as one of the most important writers in French and world literary history. The works of this period solidified Hugo's position as a leader of Romantic literature and provided the spiritual foundation for his later political activities and exile.

supporter.zh: 维克多·雨果被视为法国最伟大的作家之一，他的作品充满人道主义精神和对社会正义的不懈追求。支持者赞扬他通过文学创作揭露社会不公，为弱势群体发声，尤其是《悲惨世界》中对贫困、不公正和救赎的深刻描绘。雨果不仅是文学大师，也是坚定的共和主义者和民主斗士，他的政治立场和文学成就共同构成了19世纪法国的精神遗产。他的作品跨越时代和国界，至今仍激励着无数读者追求自由、平等和博爱。
supporter.en: Victor Hugo is regarded as one of France's greatest writers, whose works are filled with humanitarian spirit and relentless pursuit of social justice. Supporters praise him for using literature to expose social injustice and give voice to the marginalized, particularly his profound depiction of poverty, injustice, and redemption in 'Les Misérables'. Hugo was not only a literary master but also a staunch republican and democratic fighter. His political stance and literary achievements together constitute the spiritual legacy of 19th-century France. His works transcend time and borders, continuing to inspire countless readers in their pursuit of freedom, equality, and fraternity.

critic.zh: 批评者指出雨果的作品存在过度浪漫化和戏剧化的倾向，有时牺牲了现实主义深度。他的政治立场虽然高尚，但有时显得天真和理想化，对复杂现实缺乏足够认识。雨果对拿破仑三世的激烈反对导致了他近20年的流亡，这一决定虽然体现了原则性，但也使他远离了法国社会的重要变革时期。此外，一些评论家认为他的后期作品如《九十三》在艺术成就上不如早期作品，政治色彩过浓而文学性减弱。雨果的个人生活，尤其是与妻子阿黛尔长期分居而与朱丽叶·德鲁埃的公开恋情，也成为一些批评者关注的焦点。
critic.en: Critics point out that Hugo's works often tend toward excessive romanticism and dramatization, sometimes sacrificing realistic depth. While his political stance was noble, it sometimes appeared naive and idealistic, lacking sufficient understanding of complex realities. Hugo's fierce opposition to Napoleon III led to his nearly 20 years in exile, a decision that demonstrated principle but also distanced him from significant periods of French social change. Additionally, some critics argue that his later works like 'Ninety-Three' lack the artistic achievement of his earlier pieces, with excessive political coloring at the expense of literary quality. Hugo's personal life, particularly his long separation from his wife Adèle and his public affair with Juliette Drouet, has also been a focus of criticism.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，雨果被定义为19世纪法国浪漫主义文学的旗手和社会变革的象征。他的作品不仅是文学经典，也是研究19世纪法国社会、政治和历史的珍贵资料。雨果的形象超越了单纯的作家身份，成为自由、正义和反抗不公的象征符号。他的名言'即使是在最黑暗的时代，我们也要相信光明'被广泛引用，成为人类面对困境时的精神支柱。在当代，雨果的作品被不断改编为电影、音乐剧等形式，持续影响着全球流行文化。历史学者认为，雨果的成就不仅在于文学创作，更在于他通过作品塑造了公众意识，推动了社会进步，体现了知识分子的社会责任。
objective.en: In historical scholarship and popular culture, Hugo is defined as the flagbearer of 19th-century French Romantic literature and a symbol of social change. His works are not only literary classics but also valuable resources for studying 19th-century French society, politics, and history. Hugo's image transcends that of a mere writer, becoming a symbolic representation of freedom, justice, and resistance to injustice. His famous quote 'Even in the darkest times, we must believe in light' is widely cited as spiritual support for humanity facing adversity. In contemporary times, Hugo's works continue to be adapted into films, musicals, and other forms, influencing global popular culture. Historians believe that Hugo's achievements lie not only in literary creation but also in shaping public consciousness and promoting social progress through his works, embodying the social responsibility of intellectuals.

self.zh: 即使是在最黑暗的时代，我们也要相信光明。
self.en: Even in the darkest times, we must believe in light.

others.zh: 维克多·雨果是法国文学的火山，他喷发出的火焰照亮了整个世界。
others.en: Victor Hugo is a volcano of French literature, whose flames illuminate the entire world.
